variants.title: R1 — Lateral basin
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one abstract editorial artwork revision for the Transit handbook scrolling scene, portrait 2:3.
Input image 1 is a composition and material reference: the vertical falling-wave artwork. Keep its clearly downward graphite currents, warm ivory tactile paper, translucent gray shading and one slender vermilion continuity thread.
Input image 2 is a resonance geometry reference: the earlier horizontal graphite resonance illustration. Borrow its overlapping elliptical wave contours, pale nodal spaces and transparent interference bands. Do not copy its horizontal score or branching page layout.
Primary request: retain waves falling vertically, while the FORM TRANSFORMS ACROSS THE HORIZONTAL DIMENSION. Both axes must matter. Vertical currents should continuously become a broad lateral resonating field, with a transformation visible across the width, not only one narrow column that changes as it descends. Carry subtle Z-depth through oblique surfaces, folds and occlusion.
Style: richly textured graphite printmaking on warm ivory paper, extremely fine irregular contour lines, restrained translucent gray ink, faint historical echoes, airy margins. Keep the material richness of both references. Graphite and silver gray only, with one fine vermilion path.
Constraints: a single coherent continuous illustration. No labels, text, axes, chart grid, diagram arrows, panels, UI, technical schematic, literal instruments or speakers, flowers, eyes, rainbow, glow, gloss, solid 3D objects. The rings should remain open, pale and asymmetrical, never black target bullseyes. No diagram simplification. No literal waterfall, water splash or scenery. Opaque ivory background.
Revision R1 — Lateral basin.
A narrow but unmistakable cascade of vertical wave filaments enters from near the upper center-left. Preserve a long visible descending wave passage. Across the middle and lower half, these SAME filaments gradually turn and widen sideways into a broad shallow resonating membrane extending mostly toward the right and also left. Across that width, narrow waves evolve into broad elliptical contour lobes and quiet overlapping interference rings; the large membrane must span nearly the full page width. Make the connection from downward current into the lateral field continuous, not a vertical stream pasted above disconnected rings. Show the membrane at a gentle oblique angle, with a subtly raised far edge and near contours receding below it. The vermilion line descends and then follows a graceful sideways arc through the field. Keep generous open ivory pockets and only two or three dominant resonance centers. The lateral expansion should feel calm, spacious and inevitable.

Revision R2 — Crossing fields.
A long band of vertical graphite waves falls from the top through the left-center of the portrait. As it descends, portions of this same continuous wave sheet peel sideways in shallow curves across the width, meeting a softer returning fold. The crossing sheets create a broad horizontal region of delicate interference: overlapping arcs, several open elliptical nodal areas and subtle moire-like changes in line density. Make the transformation read clearly from fine vertical falling waves at the left to broad lateral interference at the right, while keeping an overall downward pull. It should look like two related rhythms finding a shared pattern, not a radial splash or separate ring stickers. Use one shallow foreground fold crossing a receding layer for Z-depth. A single thin vermilion thread travels through both the falling and lateral forms. Keep the structure asymmetrical, the centers pale, and the ink density airy.

Revision R3 — Suspended membrane.
Vertical waves descend from the upper portion into a broad suspended sheet spanning left to right through the center and lower portrait. Across the HORIZONTAL axis, the descending strands continuously deform from fine near-parallel waves into a wider vibrating saddle-like membrane, with broad lobes and narrow quiet nodal seams. The main transformation should happen across the width while the whole sheet still falls downward. Unlike concentric ripples, suggest a resonant standing-wave form through continuous bowed contour bands and alternating shallow ridges and valleys. The left and right edges drift outward and toward different depths; a delicate fold comes toward the viewer while its neighboring layer recedes. Preserve loose paper-like transparency and subtle graphite volume, not solid sculptural metal or cloth. One vermilion filament descends, then bends sideways along a lobe across the resonant surface. Keep three or four broad lobes, irregular spacing and lots of warm paper between thin lines.
